The first-run journey is recorded in rcf/discovery/journey.json, from the download to the first reply that AC-201-3 asserts, with its interruptions mapped to AC-201-4; Squire has no web design stage of its own, so a separate web journey criterion would repeat that record

Naming the Squire and its personality is a step of the first-run journey recorded in rcf/discovery/journey.json, and the reply that names the Squire is that journey's exit; Squire has no web design stage of its own, so a separate web journey criterion would repeat that record

The backup job is set up in a step of the first-run journey recorded in rcf/discovery/journey.json; the backup and the known fixes have no screen of their own in this round (the health check prints lines, the page comes later), so there is no web journey to trace

Judged: set-up's only store is its progress record, set-up.json, written whole through a file beside it, and no step is counted done until its end state is seen after it ends; a set-up killed part way is AC-201-4's own case (the step runs again from its start on the next run), so a separate crash-safety criterion would repeat AC-201-4

Judged: set-up.json is set-up's own progress record with one shape in this round, and every step checks its end state on the Mac rather than trusting the record alone; a record from an older Squire can first meet a newer one only through the signed update of REQ-014, where any migration belongs, so set-up has no stored schema to migrate

Judged: set-up runs no backup; it only writes the backup job's launchd agent, and the backup run and its observable record (backup.json and the dated archive folders) are REQ-011's, settled there, so backups are out of scope for this requirement

Judged: applies and is already AC-1101-1's: every run writes backup.json in the Squire home, which the health check reads and names when a run failed, and the backup itself is plain files in current/ and archive/<run time>/; a separate criterion would repeat AC-1101-1

Judged: the backup job never writes the owner's own files, the only data it could lose, and never deletes or overwrites a copy (an earlier copy moves to the run's archive first); a run cut short records no success, the health check names it and the next run copies again in full, which is AC-1101-1's no-partial-pass rule

Judged: the backup keeps plain copies of the owner's files in current/ and archive/<run time>/, readable without Squire, and its one record, backup.json, is a last-run report each run writes whole; there is no stored schema to migrate in this round, and a layout change would come with REQ-014's signed update
